newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria warns of bombs after threat to minister.
newsitem.headline: Austria warns of bombs after threat to minister.

text.p: The Austrian government said on Saturday it had issued a bomb warning ahead of European elections after Interior Minister Caspar Einem received a threatening letter.
Earlier this month a suspected neo-Nazi group calling itself the Bajuvarian Liberation Army (BLA) announced it would target eight prominent figures, including Chancellor Franz Vranitzky.

The interior ministry said it had taken steps to alert those named in the letter but played down the significance of the latest threats, coming a day before Austrians vote for the European parliament for the first time.
"The minister often receives this sort of mail, criticising him for being too sympathetic to foreigners," Austrian news agency APA quoted a ministry spokesman as saying.
The interior ministry said it doubted the letter to Einem was connected with the BLA -- an extremist group seeking to unite German-speaking peoples in Bavaria, the Alps and Danube River region.
The government has taken the BLA threat against Vranitzky seriously and security around the chancellor has visibly increased over the past 11 days.

The BLA has claimed responsibility for five waves of letter bombs since December, 1993. The attacks, which also spilled over into neighbouring Germany, have injured 11 people. All victims were immigrants or figures connected with immigrant issues.

Last week Einem said investigators had linked the group to the murder of four gypsies in the southeastern town of Oberwart in February 1995. The four were killed by a booby-trap bomb attached to a racist sign.
